category_title: Low-attaining students who remain quiet and passive during teacher-directed discussions
minimal_context: The student is participating in a whole-class discussion at the end of a mathematics lesson about finding possible arrangements of equal rows for 24 plants.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are finding some possible arrangements of equal rows for 24 plants in a vegetable garden. Riley, what is one way to arrange them?

STUDENT: (Puts hand up) I did two 12 times…

TUTOR: Okay. What else can you tell us about that?

STUDENT: That is all.

TUTOR: What do you think happens to the rows if we halve the 12?

STUDENT: (Sits quietly and appears attentive. He does not contribute anything else, making it difficult to conclude whether he is actually listening or simply waiting quietly for the discussion to end.)

options.A: Implement relatively tight timelines for the duration of the whole-class discussions.
options.B: Use simple language that is mathematically proper to describe arrangements or manipulations.
options.C: Adhere to a routine and provide positive reinforcement for desired behaviors during discussions.
options.D: Reduce the duration of whole-class discussions and make them more focused.
